question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Risk life and limb

options.text: In danger of death or serious injury

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3' i.e. 'In danger of death or serious injury'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Risk life and limb"** is used to refer to a situation where someone is putting themselves in a dangerous situation where they could die or get seriously hurt. (मौत या गंभीर चोट के आसार होना)

 
 
• **Example:** Firefighters often risk life and limb to save others.
 
 
 
• The phrase** "In danger of death or serious injur**y" accurately reflects the meaning of this idiom. (मृत्यु या गंभीर चोट का खतरा)
 
 
• **Example: **The man, who was hanging from a tall building, was in danger of death or serious injury.
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is - 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, **"Something that happened unexpectedly" refers to an event or occurrence which takes place without warning or preparation.(कुछ जो अनपेक्षित रूप से हुआ)
 
• **Option 2,** "Seriously ill" refers to a state of poor or weakened health condition.(गंभीर रूप से बीमार)
 
• **Option 4**, "Making unnecessary fuss" refers to a display of unnecessary excitement or concern about something relatively unimportant.(बेनियाजी शोर शराबा)
